cases.title: Ghost Buttons on iLink in all zones
cases.section_path: Metro / Metro Operator / Tests from previous Confirmation Test
cases.custom_steps:
Description

v1.3.7

Actual Result

Tapping a button on the device that does not have a corresponding top up option (ghost button) allows you to top up any iLink smartcard with a month of travel for free and it applies to the card. Top up receipt prints successfully and shows 1 Month Top Up for £0.00. The R buttons are seeming to be mirroring the functionality of the L buttons, L5 should not be pressable when topping up an iLink as it is not a Multi Journey or Travelcard.

Expected Result

The mentioned buttons should not bring up the top up confirmation screen and allow you to proceed with the top up.

Steps

Present any zone adult or child iLink to smartcard reader

Press Top Up 

Press either L5, R2, R3, R4 or R5.

Press Cash to carry out top up

Notice the top up receipt print and the Top Up Successful screen.

cases.title: TIBU-20851: TL POS Metro - Invalid top up card not detected as removed
cases.section_path: Confirmation Tests / 1.2.1
cases.custom_steps:
Link to TIBU-20851: https://flowbird.atlassian.net/browse/TIBU-20851

Description

If top-up is selected for a card that cannot be topped up then an Invalid Smartcard message is displayed. If the card is removed before this message times out to the “Please Remove Smartcard” page then the system gets stuck on the “Please Remove Smartcard” page.

From the logs it looks as if there is a null reference generated when running rule BRSetInServiceFirstPage

01-14 09:12:52:754319 [E] Transaction      [  94] BusinessRule BRSetInServiceFirstPage RunStateHandler INITIAL Exception[ System.NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.
  at Flowbird.GFTS.Features.POS.BRSetInServiceFirstPage.CheckGroupExists () [0x00001] in C:\translinkpos\POS_Features\POS.Android\Operations\Sales\BRSetInServiceFirstPage.cs:51
  at Flowbird.GFTS.Services.BusinessRules.StateMachine.BRStateMachine.RunStateHandler (System.String state) [0x00070] in C:\translinkpos\Submodules\Common\MicroServices\BusinessRules\BRFramework\BRStateMachine\BRStateMachine.cs:267  ]

Reproduction:

Present (e.g.) staff pass to reader on “Please Present Smartcard” screen

When menu shown, select “Top Up”

“Invalid Smartcard” message is shown

Remove card

Expected result

“Please Present Smartcard” screen shown

Actual result

Stays on “Invalid Smartcard” screen then times out to “Please Remove Smartcard” screen and does not timeout from this screen

Log attached

None

cases.title: TIBU-16113: POS-Performance slow
cases.section_path: Confirmation Tests / 1.2.1
cases.custom_steps:
Link to TIBU-16113: https://flowbird.atlassian.net/browse/TIBU-16113

Description

SW Version: N/A (AKA DevBuild-20230622)

The Way6 POS is observed to be going slower than expected.
A rough estimate of average time between pressing a button for a simple screen transition and the POS updating the display to show the new screen is around 5-6 seconds.

For comparison the ETM typically does the same in less than 1 second.

Timings observed:

On Un-comissioned Idle screen to ID/PIN entry screen via pressing enter key.
4.5s-6.5s

On Technician Menu screen to the Versions screen via the R2 key.
4.5s-6s

From Versions screen Back to Technician menu via the L6 'Back' key
5s

Additional observations:

Sometimes as the screen transitions a red border can be observed.
Sometimes when the screen transitions the whole screen can be seen to go black for a second.
There are no audio tones when a key is pressed and due to the slow transition speed it is often unclear whether a key press has been recognized.

Update:
The slow responsiveness is thought to be due to the way that the android solution is rendering the screen and the way we are creating and destroying activities under the hood. The Perth ETM is running on similar hardware and is also using Android and saw noticeable improvements to the UI performance when switching to the way that it has been done on the Perth Validators. The bulk of the changes made to the way the rules/activities/layouts are structured can be seen in the following PR https://bitbucket.org/parkeon-ondemand/perthpos/pull-requests/921/diffCan't find link . 


We need to try and restricted the TL POS in a similar way. Note that this work on the Perth ETM has only just been done so there may be some tweaks that need to be made.

Description

cases.title: TIBU-25073: POS > Re-presenting a different card during the Annul last transaction gets device stuck in loop
cases.section_path: Confirmation Tests / 1.3.8
cases.custom_steps:
Description

Actual : Presenting a different smartcard to the reader during the Annul Last transaction flow causes the POS to enter an error loop that requires a reboot to resolve
Expected: Exception handling should be improved here, if a different card is presented then the appropriate error screen should display and no error loop occurs
Steps:

Conduct a top-up on a smartcard (e.g. Metro MJ)

Top-up receipt prints

Present a different smartcard to the reader

Tap P button

Select Annul Previous Transaction

Device then shows the "Annulment Unsuccessful: please present the correct smartcard"

Remove the card

Select Back button; "Annulment Unsuccessful: please present the correct smartcard" screen displays again

Present a different smartcard and the "Unexpected smartcard: Please remove smartcard" screen displays

Removing the smartcard will remove the error screen but placing any smartcard on the reader will cause the same error to show

A reboot is required to resolve the issue

cases.title: TIBU-25615: TL POS: Unable to issue a topup for a Metro travelcard
cases.section_path: Confirmation Tests / 1.3.9
cases.custom_steps:
Translink have raised an issue with their test POS devices whereby they are unable to topup any Metro Travel card. This is not happening on our test POS devices, but we cannot see anything in the configuration to explain why TL are having the issue.

Logs have been obtained off their two POS’s (one running 1.3.7 and one running 1.3.8) and appear to show the same issue in the log:

09-04 16:30:51:575506 [I] Transaction      [ 491] [BRFormat09Topup] Initialises
09-04 16:30:51:605203 [E] Transaction      [ 491] [UpdateCard] Exception at line 0:
09-04 16:30:51:622137 [I] Transaction      [ 491] [BRReportStateChange] - No extra fields for this device
09-04 16:30:51:645087 [I] Transaction      [ 490] LayoutCache: Page TopUpCardFailed LAYOUTS-->ADD [ValidationFailLayout]

Full logs attached. A video is also attached showing the problem. TL topology databases are also attached.

We are hopeful that this is a configuration issue, so may need to simply debug the build using the TL topology databases so we can understand the configuration issue. 

Would also suggest we improve the logging so that we can better see what the problem is.

NOTE: This was originally raised as an issue where TL could not annul a Metro Travelcard topup, but they have subsequently found they are unable to perform the topup at all. Would therefore be good that once we fix the topup problem, we also just double check that the annulment of the topup is also successful (using the same TL topology databases)


Environment


TL Test with POS 1.3.7 and 1.3.8

Closure Reason


None
Requirements


GIVEN I have presented a Metro Travelcard for topup
WHEN I select a topup and press CASH
THEN The topup should be successful

cases.title: TIBU-26905: TL POS : Add ability to manually adjust Ethernet network settings from Technician Menu
cases.section_path: Confirmation Tests / 1.3.10
cases.custom_steps:
Description

Background: The Metro POS will be connected via Ethernet in their install locations, connected through the Translink corporate network. Each POS will be allocated an IP address (including a gateway, subnet mask and DNS). On our test POS devices set for INTEGRATION mode, these values are currently being configured by going into the state configuration during bootup and setting each one individually. 

However on live devices, they will bet set in PRODUCTION mode with no ability to go into the state configuration during bootup, and so an alternative means is needed to be able to configure the Ethernet settings.

Request: A Technician will need to be able to adjust the network settings. Once a Technician signs in, they will click on the “Network Settings” option R1 on screen 11 (Technician Menu board 12) of the UX found here:

Made with Overflow 

This will take them to screen 11.1.8. Note that this screen does not need to display the cellular details at this moment because Metro does not require cellular. A modified version of this screen is shown below:

NetworkSettingsSummary.png
The Technician will then click on the L2 button to access the Ethernet settings as shown on screen 11.2.10 of the UX, but modified as shown below (note the additional DNS value, and the ability to change using R5):

NetworkSettingsEthernet.jpg
Clicking on the “Change” R6 button will enable the fields for editing. 

- Clicking L1 will select the IP adddress field
- Clicking L2 will select the Subnet Mask field
- Clicking L3 will select the Default Gateway field
- Clicking L4 will select the DNS field

The numeric entry buttons can be used. The * key will act as a “point” (note if this is not possible, then we will expect a keyboard to be plugged in to modify these settings).

When the “Change” R6 button is pressed, and the fields are enabled for editing, the button text will change to show “Save”.

Clicking the “Save” button will update the Ethernet settings as per below:

/system/network/address : this should be set as per the “IP address” field
/system/network/dns : this should be set as per the “DNS” field
/system/network/gateway: this should be set as per the “Default Gateway” field
/system/network/mask : this should be set as per the “Subnet Mask” field

Clicking the “Save” R6 button will also disable the fields for editing, and change the button text back to showing “Change”

Environment


GIVEN The POS is configured for PRODUCTION mode
WHEN The POS is commissioned
THEN The Technician needs to be able to change the Ethernet settings

cases.title: TIBU-13180: As a POS Operator I want my device to be capable of printing a barcode on a ticket
cases.section_path: Confirmation Tests / 2.0.X
cases.custom_steps:
Description

If the “Print Barcode” product setting for the product that is being purchased is set to true then a multiple use barcode should be printed at the end of the ticket. If it is false then a barcode is not printed on the ticket and there should be no white space at the end of the ticket for where the barcode could have gone. This is required for both bus and rail ticket issues.

The only exception to the above rule is if a group ticket (multiple passengers on one ticket) is purchased. In this case a barcode should not be printed on the ticket regardless of the “Print Barcode” product setting.

Note that the gap between the end of the ticket and the barcode should be roughly as shown in the Multiple Use Barcode specification.

The barcode itself should be encoded with all of the product information that corresponds to the ticket that is being purchased.

All of the travel tickets (i.e. tickets purchased using cash, card or warrant) including concession/half fare purchases but not smartcard topups/issues should have the functionality to print the barcode on the end if configured to do so. The only other exceptions to this are family tickets which will not require the barcode on the end of the template.

Note that this functionality has already been delivered on TVM (bus and rail) and HHD (Glider and rail) and at least some of the logic for encoding and printing the barcodes should be able to reused from common. The biggest thing will probably be updating the current formats to have the optional barcode on the end - HHD is probably the best example of how we want this to be done.

The audit record sent to CloudFare for the ticket purchase must also be updated to include the BarcodeID that’s encoded in the printed barcode in the TransactionProducts section of the audit

Environment


None
Acceptance Criteria
SCENARIO 1

GIVEN I have selected a ticket that is configured to print a barcode

AND the ticket is not a group ticket

WHEN that ticket is purchased

THEN the corresponding ticket is printed

AND at the end of the ticket a multiple use barcode is printed

AND the gap between the end of the ticket and the barcode matches the specified size

AND the data encoded in the barcode corresponds to the ticket that has been issued

AND the unique id from the barcode encoding is audited in the BarcodeId field in the audit data

SCENARIO 2

GIVEN I have selected a ticket that is not configured to print a barcode

WHEN that ticket is purchased

THEN the corresponding ticket is printed

AND at the end of the ticket a multiple use barcode is not printed

AND the unique id from the barcode encoding is NOT audited in the BarcodeId field in the audit data

SCENARRIO 3

GIVEN I have selected a ticket that is configured to print a barcode

AND the ticket is a group ticket

WHEN that ticket is purchased

THEN the corresponding ticket is printed

AND at the end of the ticket a multiple use barcode is not printed

AND the unique id from the barcode encoding is NOT audited in the BarcodeId field in the audit data

Closure Reason

cases.title: TIBU-13513: [Post Hub] Application must be able to store an array of encryption keys and encrypt a barcode using the right key
cases.section_path: Confirmation Tests / 2.0.X
cases.custom_steps:
Description

In order to support some amount of key rollover in the future, the application must be able to store an array of encryption keys (the idea being that if the current one is compromised then a software update can be put out that sets an expiry date for the current key and adds a second key to the array with a longer expiry date) that are each assigned a Key Version Code (to identify which one to use when decrypting the barcode) and an Expiry Date.

When encrypting a barcode the encryption must be done using the key with the longest expiry date and the corresponding Key Version Code should be added to the barcode data for later validation.

Note that the keys should be different between test and production environments.

This story should also store the first key that will be used in the test and production environments.

Note that this functionality has already been implemented on the HHD and GV (which are other Android devices) so hopefully the logic can be lifted from there for the POS. The device should use the Barcode Data file configured in TMS to get the keys for encrypting the barcode data.

cases.title: TIBU-22963: TL POS Rail - Confirm process for cellular connection/configuration
cases.section_path: Confirmation Tests / 2.0.X
cases.custom_steps:
Key details
Description

Unclear if this is a bug/something that requires a code change or whether this is something we are missing in the configuration setup.

The majority of TL POS' will be cellular connected, but we are struggling to get a TL POS setup and successfully connected using cellular. This is both with the test POS' here in Poole and also 2 test POS' over in Belfast.

After speaking with Paul Brine, he has confirmed the Way6+Android does definitely connect to cellular as he has had his devices successfully setup. However when following the same setup process, our TL Way6 POS' do not have a cellular connection.

This needs checking, to understand why the TL Way6 POS is not connecting to cellular and to make sure there isn’t something in the application code causing the problem. For example when going to Network Settings, there is no information for cellular but believed this is somewhat expected because cellular is not configured through the NetworkConfigurationService I am lead to believe.

The following shows how we have the modem settings configured, note that this is a TL SIM hence the EE APN/username/password settings. Also note that we have ethernet disabled (enable set to 0) because there is apparently a known issue where if ethernet is enabled/connected then Android will not use cellular.

{
    "modem": {
        "enable": "1",
        "logs": {
            "enable": "0",
            "maxSize": "300",
            "port": "/dev/ttyUSB0"
        },
        "restart": {
            "delayBeforeRestarting": "300",
            "enable": "0",
            "loggingUntilRestart": {
                "enable": "0"
            },
            "minRestartDelay": "14400",
            "observedAlarms": ""
        },
        "sim": {
            "apn": "everywhere",
            "password": "secure",
            "pin": "",
            "user": "eesecure"
        },
        "temperature": {
            "alarmThreshold": "80",
            "checkPeriod": "300",
            "enableConfiguration": "1"
        }
    }
}

Environment


None
Acceptance Criteria


None
Closure Reason


None
Requirements


GIVEN The POS is configured to use cellular
WHEN The POS is powered on with a valid SIM
THEN The POS should communicate over cellular

cases.title: TIBU-27664 - POS v.1.3.10 > Randomly went Comms Locked
cases.section_path: Confirmation Tests / 1.3.11
cases.custom_steps:
Version: v1.3.10

Actual: E.g.1. When placing an child iLink zone 3, the POS was showing flakey performance and flickering between Please Remove Smartcard and the smart card menu then got put into a Communications Locked state.

Expected: Child iLink Zone 3 issuing should not put the POS into a Communications Locked state.

Steps: (E.g.1)

Place Child iLink Zone 3 on smart card reader

Select the 1 day issue option and confirm payment using cash

Lift smartcard off and then back on

Notice how the POS will flicker between screens and then go into a Comms Locked state.

E.g.1: Issue occurred around on device 990 at 14:32 on 2/12/25 - please see logs below:

https://parkeontranslink.sharepoint.com/:f:/s/Translink%20Ticketing%20System%20Replacement%20Project/IgDNl6hD4ab7S4Ep_Q2A9AmeAconbzY1KSbeFkGExSssNZQ?e=QfWeb3Connect your OneDrive account 

E.g.2 Steps:

Top-Up a expired DayLink with 5 Days 

Re-present smartcard

Press P

Press Annul Previous Transaction

POS went into Comms Lock

15:32 

Logs: 043990_Logs_DayLinkCommsLock_021225: https://parkeontranslink.sharepoint.com/:f:/s/Translink%20Ticketing%20System%20Replacement%20Project/IgDXChJ1Y7K6Ta42QNCkJocSASqA-jCqG_i06jUCgolqN-8?e=8d1HZRConnect your OneDrive account 

E.g. 3: Actual: POS randomly went comms locked when attempting to wake up screen. The device had been power cycled a couple of times earlier in the day to capture logs

Expected: POS should not go comms locked when attempting to wake up screen

Issue occurred at roughly 14:45/50 on 043984 on 02/12. See logs below: https://parkeontranslink.sharepoint.com/:f:/s/Translink%20Ticketing%20System%20Replacement%20Project/IgCpLWpHbWjQTbMokohbWIUoAaXUSDja_36OJoBSN8ZVpeM?e=WQ28BwConnect your OneDrive account

cases.section_path: Delete
cases.custom_steps:
Description

When Printing a Cross Border Ticket the price displayed on the ticket is incorrect

Steps to Reproduce:
- Sign in as an operator and go to the Rail FLU Screen
- Purchase and Print a XB Ticket (example: 1 - Yorkgate to 62 Dundalk CIV)
- The Price on the Ticket is Showing “${PriceGBP}EURO}”

NOTE: This is the same weather the ticket is a single, a weekly or a 3 monthly

Acceptance criteria:
GIVEN An Operator is signed on and on the Rail FLU Screen
WHEN a Cross Border Ticket is purchased and Printed
THEN the price given on the Ticket should be correct
